MoodRhythm is a smartphone and web application designed to support patients diagnosed with bipolar disorder in tracking their health over a long period, using both automatic and manual tracking of symptoms

MoodRhythm, an app for tracking and monitoring sleep and social activity, can be used to detect mood changes, and can be used to improve the quality of life for patients with bipolar disorder, and can be further developed to help patients and clinicians in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physiological computing has the potential to transform the way we diagnose and treat psychiatric disorders.
we are developing a new paradigm for monitoring and treating psychiatric illnesses.
the use of physiological sensors and data in psychiatry could help us move from broad categories of diagnoses to a more personalized approach to diagnosis and treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physiological computing is not just a tool for detecting psychiatric illness but also a way to tailor treatment to individual characteristics of the illness.

the physiological computing community can play an important role in helping people suffering from serious mental illnesses by developing systems that can help patients and clinicians detect the onset of mood episodes and provide feedback that can help them stabilize their mood and lead healthier lives.
physiological computing can be used as a powerful tool for developing systems that help detect and capitalize on the biological dimensions of psychiatric illness.
